note.text: Rail transport runs on fixed tracks and needs stations or terminals, signalling, maintenance and suitable rolling stock. It can move large flows along established corridors, but goods may still need road transport at the ends. Gradients, construction costs, demand and connections affect development. Rail is not automatically suitable for every small or scattered flow.

sections.heading: Your goal and connections
sections.text: By the end, you should be able to explain rail’s infrastructure requirements and compute freight tonne-kilometres. Builds on: road transport and networks. Leads to: comparison of transport impacts.

sections.heading: Follow the local example or model
sections.text: Camrail’s network description includes Douala–Yaoundé and Yaoundé–Ngaoundéré connections. No timetable or current capacity is assumed here. In a fictional freight record, {20} tonnes travel {50} km. The work measured as freight tonne-kilometres is {20*50}, not a count of passengers, vehicles or money.

sections.heading: Apply and check
sections.text: Identify the flow and corridor, then examine terminal access and transfer needs. For freight tonne-kilometres multiply tonnes by kilometres. Do not add different units or interpret the result as tonnes of goods alone.
